newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SENNA PROSECUTION DISMISS DEBRIS CLAIM.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SENNA PROSECUTION DISMISS DEBRIS CLAIM.

text.p: An Italian public prosecutor on Monday dismissed suggestions that debris on the Imola race track may have caused the death of Brazilian Formula One driver Ayrton Senna, Ansa news agency reported.

Prosecutor Maurizio Passarini, who is leading investigations into the fatal crash at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, told Ansa he still believed that Senna's Williams team was to blame for the accident.
The Sunday Times newspaper published a photograph at the weekend showing a small piece of debris in the path of Senna's car moments before it crashed into a wall.
Passarini dismissed the paper's suggestion that the Brazilian might have died because he lost control of his Williams car after trying to avoid the unidentified fragment.

"Even if the photograph is admitted as evidence, it won't change the prosecutors' opinion by one millimetre, which has indicated that the snapped steering column caused the Senna accident," Passarini was quoted as saying.

Team chief Frank Williams and five other people go on trial in Imola on Thursday charged with manslaughter over Senna's death. Prosecutors believe the steering column broke because of a faulty modification.
"The prosecutors are convinced that they have isolated the cause of the accident," Passarini said. "In any case the trial will have the last word," he added.
Thursday's opening session is expected to be purely technical. Witnesses are not due to give evidence until March.
The Sunday Times said the tiny piece of blue debris may have come from a collision between a Benetton car and a Lotus at the start of the race.
